# RNAseq Quality Control

```{r set_qc_cuts}

# Set quality control cut-offs
alignCut = 75
totalReadsCut = 1
medianCVCut = 0.8

# Determine which libraries pass quality control based on QC thresholds
design$qcPass <- design$fastq_total_reads > totalReadsCut*10^6 &
  design$pct_aligned > alignCut &
  design$median_cv_coverage < medianCVCut

```


# Gene filtering and normalization of protein coding genes

```{r protein_coding_genes}

# Keep protein coding genes with MGNC symbols; drop non-protein-coding genes
# v38 <- annotables::grcm38 # Name changed from grcm38 to grcm39 on new version 8/21/2026
v38 <- annotables::grcm39
pc38 <- v38[v38$biotype == "protein_coding",] # get protein coding genes 
pcNoSymbol <- pc38[pc38$symbol == "",] 
pcWithSymbol <- pc38[pc38$symbol != "",] 

# Subset rawcountsQC to those with MGNC symbol
rawcountsWithSymbol <- rawcountsQC[rownames(rawcountsQC) %in% pcWithSymbol$ensgene,]
dim(rawcountsWithSymbol) 

rawcountsWithSymbol <- as.data.frame(rawcountsWithSymbol)

# Add column called "gene" containing MGNC symbol from pcWith symbol
rawcountsWithSymbol$gene <- pcWithSymbol$symbol[match(rownames(rawcountsWithSymbol),
                                                            pcWithSymbol$ensgene)]
dim(rawcountsWithSymbol) 

# Aggregate/sum counts for duplicated MGNC symbols]
pcRawcounts <- rawcountsWithSymbol %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gene) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(across(starts_with("lib"), sum)) %>% 
  arrange(gene) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble:: column_to_rownames("gene") # removed gene column and made it rownames
dim(pcRawcounts) 

```

```{r gene_filtering}

# Helper function to filter lowly-expressed genes
gene_filter_func <- function(counts_in, 
                             minlib_pct = 0.1, # % of total libs
                             minCPM = 1){ # minimum num CPM
 
  normCPM <- as.data.frame(t(t(counts_in*10^6)/colSums(counts_in))) # normalize counts to cpm

  # If normCPM is greater/equal to the minCPM & greater/equal to the minlib_pct, keep gene
  keepGenes <- rowSums(normCPM >= minCPM) >= minlib_pct*ncol(normCPM)
  filteredGenes <- counts_in[keepGenes,]
  filteredGenes <- drop_na(filteredGenes)
  
  return(filteredGenes)
 
}

# Run the function on data frame to filter out genes with low expression
pcCountsFiltered <- gene_filter_func(pcRawcounts, 0.1, 1)
dim(pcCountsFiltered)

```

```{r norm_filtered_rawcounts}

# Function to normalize filtered counts using tmm for bulk RNAseq or deconvolution for large scRNAseq datasets 
normalize_counts_func <- function(counts_in, method){
   
     if(method == "decon"){
    # Normalize using the deconvolution algorithm
         decon_norm_factors = scran::computeSumFactors(as.matrix(counts_in))
         counts_norm = as.data.frame(t(t(counts_in)/decon_norm_factors))
         }
    if(method == "tmm"){
        dge <- DGEList(counts_in)
        dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
        counts_norm <- cpm(dge, normalized.lib.sizes=TRUE)
        }
  
  return(counts_norm)
}

# Normalize counts
pcCountsNorm <- as.data.frame(normalize_counts_func(pcCountsFiltered, "tmm"))

```

# Principal component analysis (PCA)

```{r run_pca}

#Run PCA on the normalized log2 transformed counts data
pca <- prcomp(log2(as.data.frame(t(pcCountsNorm))+1), center=TRUE, scale=FALSE) 

var <- get_pca_var(pca)
head(var$coord) # preview coordinates for variation

pca_contributions <- as.data.frame((var$contrib)) # Contributions of each pca to variation

# Get summary info of pca importance of components
pcaSum <- summary(pca)

pca_variance <- as.data.frame(t(pcaSum$importance))
pca_variance$pc <- factor(row.names(pca_variance), levels = mixedsort(row.names(pca_variance)))

pcaScores <- as.data.frame(pca$x)
pcaScores$libid <- row.names(pcaScores)

# Merge design QC with pcaScores and export as csv
pcaScores <- merge(designQC, pcaScores, by.x = "libid", by.y = "row.names")
pc1Lab <- paste("PC1 (", round(100*pcaSum$importance[2, 1], 1),  "%)", sep="")
pc2Lab <- paste("PC2 (", round(100*pcaSum$importance[2, 2], 1),  "%)", sep="")
pc3Lab <- paste("PC3 (", round(100*pcaSum$importance[2, 3], 1),  "%)", sep="")
pc4Lab <- paste("PC4 (", round(100*pcaSum$importance[2, 4], 1),  "%)", sep="")
pc5Lab <- paste("PC5 (", round(100*pcaSum$importance[2, 5], 1),  "%)", sep="")
pc6Lab <- paste("PC6 (", round(100*pcaSum$importance[2, 6], 1),  "%)", sep="")

#PC correlation matrix
corrMat_colNames <- c("genotype", "treatment", "timepoint", "mouseID",
                      "tophatstats_total_reads", "median_cv_coverage", "mapped_paired_reads", 
                      "percent_duplication", "pct_aligned", "fastq_total_reads", "mapped_reads")

pcaCors <- designQC[, corrMat_colNames]

for(col in corrMat_colNames) {
  pcaCors[[col]] = as.numeric(as.factor(pcaCors[[col]]))
}


# Compute correlations between PCA scores and each metadata variable
pcaCors <- apply(pca$x , 2, function(pc) {
  sapply(pcaCors, function(var) cor(pc, var, use = "complete.obs",  method = "pearson"))
})

pcaCors
```

# DGE analysis 

```{r functions_for_differential_analysis}

#Make functions to streamline DGE analysis for multiple comparisons

#Function to add category/change (i.e. up, down, ns) column to de genes DF
categorize <- function(object, regulationCategories, logFC_cutoff = 1, p_cutoff = 0.05) {
  object$change <- regulationCategories[3]
  object$change[object$logFC >= +logFC_cutoff & object$adj.P.Val < p_cutoff] <- regulationCategories[1]
  object$change[object$logFC <= -logFC_cutoff & object$adj.P.Val < p_cutoff] <- regulationCategories[2]
  object$change <- factor(object$change, levels = regulationCategories)
  
  return(object)
}

```

```{r define_empty_variables}

# Make empty variables for different comparisons/models
designMat <- list()
vwts <- list()
contrasts <- list()
contrastCoefs <- list()
vfit <- list()
corfit <- list()
vfitEB <- list()
topTables <- list()

```

## Cell-means model (all conditions model)

A cell-means model estimates one coefficient per experimental condition, representing the mean expression of that condition, and all biological questions are answered by contrasts between those means.

Once the means are estimated, can test: 1) treatment effects, 2) genotype effects, 3) interactions, and 4) time-specific differences

```{r define_all_conditions_model}

# DGE cutoffs
logfc_cutoff <- 1
p_cutoff <- 0.05

# Name model and create folders
modelName <- "all_conditions"
folderName <- modelName

dir.create(file.path(dirTables, folderName), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(dirPlots, folderName), showWarnings = FALSE)

#Subset designQC if needed
designModel <- designQC #no need to subset in this case

#Create single combined factor for each group    
designModel$genotype_timepoint <- paste0(designModel$genotype, "_", designModel$timepoint)

unique(designModel$genotype_timepoint)

designModel$genotype_timepoint <- factor(designModel$genotype_timepoint,
                                         levels = c("WT_0h", "WT_6h",
                                                    "WT_24h", "WT_48h",
                                                    "IRF5ko_0h", "IRF5ko_6h",      
                                                    "IRF5ko_24h", "IRF5ko_48h"))

modelCounts <- pcCountsNorm[ , designModel$libid]


#Define model matrix 
designMat[[modelName]] <- model.matrix(~ 0 + genotype_timepoint, data = designModel)

#Look at column names of designMat and simplify names so contrasts are easier to make later
print(colnames(designMat[[modelName]]))

colnames(designMat[[modelName]]) <- colnames(designMat[[modelName]]) %>%
  str_remove_all("genotype_timepoint") 
print(colnames(designMat[[modelName]]))

```

## Linear model

```{r run_de_analysis_all_conditions_model}

# Run the differential expression analysis; include donor mouse (mouseID) as random effect
# 1. Calculate the voom weights
vwts[[modelName]]  <- voomWithQualityWeights(modelCounts, design = designMat[[modelName]], plot = T, span = 0.1)

# 1.a. include mouse as random effect in limma
# https://support.bioconductor.org/p/59700/
corfit[[modelName]] <-  duplicateCorrelation(vwts[[modelName]],
                        design = designMat[[modelName]],
                        block = designModel$mouseID)
corfit[[modelName]]$consensus.correlation 

# 1.b rerun voom
vwts[[modelName]] <- voomWithQualityWeights(modelCounts,
                                            design= designMat[[modelName]],
                                            block = designModel$mouseID,
                                            correlation = corfit[[modelName]]$consensus,
                                            plot = F)

# 2. with donor effect
vfit[[modelName]] <- lmFit(vwts[[modelName]], design = designMat[[modelName]],
                           block = designModel$mouseID,
                           correlation = corfit[[modelName]]$consensus)
vfit[[modelName]] <- eBayes(vfit[[modelName]])

# 3. Calculate contrast coefficients
contrasts[[modelName]] <- makeContrasts(
  # WT response to R848 vs. baseline
  WT_6h  - WT_0h,
  WT_24h - WT_0h,
  WT_48h - WT_0h,
  # WT responses to R848 at different times
  WT_24h - WT_6h,
  WT_48h - WT_6h,
  WT_48h - WT_24h,
  # IRF5ko response to R848 vs. baseline
  IRF5ko_6h  - IRF5ko_0h,
  IRF5ko_24h - IRF5ko_0h,
  IRF5ko_48h - IRF5ko_0h,
  # IRF5ko responses to R848 at different times
  IRF5ko_24h - IRF5ko_6h,
  IRF5ko_48h - IRF5ko_6h,
  IRF5ko_48h - IRF5ko_24h,
  # Genotype differences at each timepoint
  WT_0h - IRF5ko_0h,
  WT_6h  - IRF5ko_6h,
  WT_24h - IRF5ko_24h,
  WT_48h - IRF5ko_48h,
  # Interaction: genotype-dependent R848 responses
  R848_response_genotype_diff_6h = WT_6h - WT_0h - IRF5ko_6h + IRF5ko_0h,
  R848_response_genotype_diff_24h = WT_24h - WT_0h - IRF5ko_24h + IRF5ko_0h,
  R848_response_genotype_diff_48h = WT_48h - WT_0h - IRF5ko_48h + IRF5ko_0h,
  levels = designMat[[modelName]])

contrastCoefs[[modelName]] <- contrasts.fit(vfit[[modelName]], contrasts[[modelName]])

# 4. Correct for multiple testing (FDR) using empirical Bayes function
vfitEB[[modelName]] <- eBayes(contrastCoefs[[modelName]])

```

```{r parse_contrasts_all_conditions_model}

contrastSummary <- data.frame(name = colnames(contrasts[[modelName]]))

# Initialize studyGroup and refGroup as NA
contrastSummary$studyGroup <- NA
contrastSummary$refGroup <- NA

# Make logical vector, simple contrast pattern: exactly one " - " (space-hyphen-space)
simpleContrastIdx <- grepl("^[^\\-]+ - [^\\-]+$", contrastSummary$name)

# For simple contrasts, extract study and ref groups
contrastSummary$studyGroup[simpleContrastIdx] <- sapply(
  strsplit(contrastSummary$name[simpleContrastIdx], " - "),
  `[`, 1)

contrastSummary$refGroup[simpleContrastIdx] <- sapply(
  strsplit(contrastSummary$name[simpleContrastIdx], " - "),
  `[`, 2)

# For interaction / complex contrasts
interactionNames <- c("R848_response_genotype_diff_6h", 
                      "R848_response_genotype_diff_24h", 
                      "R848_response_genotype_diff_48h")

for(intName in interactionNames){
  idx <- contrastSummary$name == intName
  
  # Extract timepoint from the name
  time <- sub("R848_response_genotype_diff_", "", intName)
  
  # Assign intuitive response-based study and ref groups
  contrastSummary$studyGroup[idx] <- paste0("WT_response_", time)
  contrastSummary$refGroup[idx]   <- paste0("IRF5ko_response_", time)
}
print(contrastSummary)

# format everything a bit nicer
contrastSummary$printName <- paste0(contrastSummary$studyGroup, " vs. ",
                                    contrastSummary$ refGroup)

print(contrastSummary)

```

```{r write_out_top_genes_all_conditions_model}

# Write out the top genes for each comparison
for (iContrast in 1:ncol(contrastCoefs[[modelName]])) {
  contrastName <- colnames(contrastCoefs[[modelName]])[iContrast]

  top.table <- topTable(vfitEB[[modelName]], coef = iContrast, sort.by = "P", n = Inf)
  setDT(top.table, keep.rownames = "gene")
  
  top.table <- categorize(top.table, enrichmentCategories, logFC_cutoff = logfc_cutoff, p_cutoff = p_cutoff)
  
  top.table_ <- dplyr::select(top.table, -"t", -"B")
  
  #change to three significant digits
  top.table_$AveExpr <- signif(top.table_$AveExpr, digits = 3)
  top.table_$P.Value <- signif(top.table_$P.Value, digits = 3)
  top.table_$adj.P.Val <- signif(top.table_$adj.P.Val, digits = 3)
  top.table_$logFC <- signif(top.table_$logFC, digits = 3)

  #change column names
  top.table_ <- top.table_ %>%
      dplyr::rename(log2FC = logFC,
                    p.Value = P.Value)
  
  out_file <- paste0("DEgenes_", contrastName, ".csv")
  out_file_path <- file.path(dirTables, folderName, out_file)
  
  write.csv(top.table_,
            out_file_path,
            row.names = F,
            quote=F)

  top.table$contrast <- contrastName
  
  topTables[[modelName]][[contrastName]] = top.table
}

```

## Scatterplots for effect size, each timepoint

Want scatterplot looking at effect size of NT vs. R848 for each genotype, logFC in for WT on x-axis on logFC for IRF5ko on y-axis. Color by up in WT only, up in IRF5ko only, up in both genotypes, or ns/down

### 6h timepoint

```{r combine_topTables_genotype_6hvs0h_for_plot}

# Assign individual variables for each topTable combo for readibility downstream
tt6hWT <-  topTables[["all_conditions"]][["WT_6h - WT_0h"]]
tt6hKO <-  topTables[["all_conditions"]][["IRF5ko_6h - IRF5ko_0h"]]

# Merge the two top tables for genotype based on gene
tt6hCombined <- merge(tt6hWT[, c("gene", "logFC", "adj.P.Val", "change")],
                      tt6hKO[, c("gene", "logFC", "adj.P.Val", "change")], 
                      by = "gene", suffixes = c("_WT", "_IRF5ko"))

# Add column for whether gene is up in WT, IRF5ko, or both
tt6hCombined <- tt6hCombined %>%
  dplyr::mutate(upClass = case_when(change_WT == "up" & change_IRF5ko != "up" ~ "up_WT",
                                    change_WT != "up" & change_IRF5ko == "up" ~ "up_IRF5ko",
                                    change_WT == "up" & change_IRF5ko == "up" ~ "up_both",
                                    TRUE ~ "ns_or_down"),

                                                     "up_IRF5ko", 
                                                     "up_both", 
                                                     "ns_or_down")))
```

```{r heatmap_R848_upGenes_WT_allTps_allConditions_model}

# Make heatmaps that span all samples
sig_genes <- upGenesWTallTp

design_ <- designModel

reorder <- order(design_$genotype, design_$timepoint, 
                 design_$mouseID, design_$libid)

design_ <- design_[reorder, ]
  
colSplit <- design_$genotype

pcCountsNorm_ <- pcCountsNorm[ , design_$libid]

counts_ <- pcCountsNorm_[rownames(pcCountsNorm_) %in% sig_genes, ]

labels <- row.names(counts_)

tp <- t(scale(t(log2(1+counts_))))

ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(genotype = design_$genotype,
                        timepoint = design_$timepoint,
                        col = colors)

# Plot with no gene names
hm <- Heatmap(tp, 
             show_column_names = FALSE, 
             show_row_names = FALSE, 
             row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6),
             cluster_columns = FALSE, 
             name = "row z-score", 
             top_annotation = ha, 
             col = col_fun, 
             cluster_rows = TRUE, 
             column_title = "R848-upregulated genes in WT cells only, all times",
             column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
             show_row_dend = FALSE,
             column_split = colSplit,
             heatmap_legend_param = list(legend_direction = "horizontal"))

hm <- draw(hm, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")

# Export plot 
pdf(file.path(dirPlots, folderName, "hm_R848_upregGenes_WT_alltimes_lfcCut1pVal0.05_noGeneNames.pdf"), 
    height = 6, width = 6)
print(hm)
invisible(dev.off())

```

```{r some_genesLabeled_heatmap_R848_upGenes_WT_and_up_iHPCsig_genes}

# Make heatmap that span all samples
sig_genes <- upGenesWTiHPCsig
design_ <- designModel

reorder <- order(design_$genotype, design_$timepoint, 
                 design_$mouseID, design_$libid)

design_ <- design_[reorder, ]
  
colSplit <- design_$genotype

pcCountsNorm_ <- pcCountsNorm[ , design_$libid]

counts_ <- pcCountsNorm_[rownames(pcCountsNorm_) %in% sig_genes, ]

labels <- row.names(counts_)

tp <- t(scale(t(log2(1+counts_))))

ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(genotype = design_$genotype,
                        timepoint = design_$timepoint,
                        col = colors,
                        show_legend = c(genotype = FALSE, timepoint = FALSE), # Suppress legends for both annotations
                        show_annotation_name = FALSE) 

genesToLabel <- c("Batf", "C1qb", "Cd300c2", "Cd72", "Ets2", "Fcgr4", "Fth1",
                  "Il10", "Il16", "Il18bp", "Itga9", "Bcl2a1b", "Ccr7", "Il12b",
                  "Mertk", "Pecam1", "C1qa", "Cxcr5")

# Get the row indices of your genes of interest
geneRowIdx <- which(rownames(tp) %in% genesToLabel)

# Create the row annotation with anno_mark()
geneAnno <- rowAnnotation(genes = anno_mark(at = geneRowIdx,
                                            labels = rownames(tp)[geneRowIdx],
                                            labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8, 
                                                             fontface = "italic"),  # style the text
                                            link_width = unit(5, "mm")))   # length of the connecting line

hm <- Heatmap(tp, 
             show_column_names = FALSE, 
             show_row_names = FALSE, 
             right_annotation = geneAnno,
             cluster_columns = FALSE, 
             name = "row z-score", 
             top_annotation = ha, 
             col = col_fun, 
             cluster_rows = TRUE, 
             column_title = "R848-upregulated (WT cells) & upregulated splenic iHPC genes, log2FC > 1",
             column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9),
             show_row_dend = FALSE,
             column_split = colSplit,
             heatmap_legend_param = list(legend_direction = "horizontal"))

hm <- draw(hm, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")


#Export plot with the select gene names
pdf(file.path(dirPlots, folderName,
              "hm_R848_upregGenes_WT_alltimes_and_spliHPCupreg_lfcCut1pVal0.05_selectGeneNames_noLegend.pdf"), 
    height = 5, width = 6) 
print(hm)
invisible(dev.off())

```
